title: Avro Lancaster PB366 - Cross
memorial_details: The cross is a plain white wooden cross, about 1.2 m high, at the junction of Dovecote Lane and High Street (B1043) in Great Paxton. The cross member reads LANCASTER CRASH 1944, and a board beneath gives the date, the aircraft and 35 Squadron. IWM records it in good condition. IWM gives no maker or date for it, and none of the other sources read says who put it up.
inscription: Cross: LANCASTER CRASH 1944. Board: CHRISTMAS EVE 44/ LANCASTER PB366/ 35 SQUADRON

Memorial planned to honour crew of tragic bomber

narrative:
Lancaster III PB366 (TL-S) of 35 Squadron, a Pathfinder squadron, took off from Graveley at 15:35 on 24 December 1944 for Cologne. Ten of the squadron's aircraft were detailed to attack the Nippes Marshalling Yard. PB366's Pathfinder role was Supporter.

FIDO fog dispersal was burning at take-off. PB366 crashed almost immediately, flying into trees at Great Paxton. The squadron-association page puts the crash site at Low Farm, about half a mile south of the aerodrome. AM Form 1180 blamed the pilot losing control in fog through faulty instrument flying. All seven crew died.

The bombs were thrown clear of the wreck. One rolled into the wall of the farmhouse bathroom at Low Farm, with the farmer's wife inside, and did not explode. A man on the Graveley crash guard reached the scene a few minutes later and found the aircraft burning.

The crew were Flying Officer Arthur Kenyon (pilot, 23), Sergeant Leonard Williams (flight engineer, 23), Sergeant Albert Thomas (navigator, 22), Flight Sergeant Alec Cousins (bomb aimer, 21), Flight Sergeant Cecil Blundell (wireless operator, 20), Sergeant Cyril Winter (mid-upper gunner, 23) and Sergeant Roy Yallop (rear gunner, 24), named as Roy Frederick Arthur Yallop by IBCC and Aircrew Remembered and as Roy Arthur Yallop by the RAF Graveley site. Their burial places run from Prestwich and Staveley to Ystalyfera, Maidenhead, Southampton, Harlington and Ipswich. Thomas's age is given by Aircrew Remembered only; IBCC and CWGC do not state it, and the Graveley PDF shows a question mark.

Yallop had flown as a gunner with the Potts crew on the Gremberg daylight raid on 23 December, the day before he died. His family received the telegram on Christmas morning.

external_narratives.summary: Crew page with take-off time, FIDO, crew table (rank, role, age, service number, burial, parents), a biography of Sgt Yallop and a note on the planned Great Paxton memorial. Compiled with research by Linda Ibrom and credits Bomber Command Losses, CWGC and family photos.
key_details: Crew of seven table with ages and burials
Yallop flew the Gremberg raid on 23 Dec with the Potts crew

external_narratives.summary: Earlier write-up of the loss: crew list with service numbers, burials, Yallop biography, his poem, and a 1985 account by a member of the Graveley crash guard. Aircrew Remembered's crew page may draw on it; they are counted as separate publishers here but not as fully independent.
key_details: Crash guard account: Low Farm, bomb hit farmhouse bathroom
Navigator's age shown as a question mark

external_narratives.summary: Squadron-association loss page quoting the operations record book, AM Form 1180 and eyewitness notes. Gives the target, load, Pathfinder role, FIDO confirmation, the accident finding and crash site.
key_details: Ten 35 Sqn aircraft detailed for Nippes Marshalling Yard
AM Form 1180: pilot lost control on take-off in fog, faulty instrument flying
Crash site Low Farm, half a mile south of the aerodrome

external_narratives.summary: IBCC record for the flight engineer, with raid context (102 aircraft, 7 lost), crash site, CWGC number, and the list of six memorials including the roadside cross and the Holy Trinity memorial.
key_details: Lists 'Roadside cross and board, Great Paxton' and Holy Trinity memorial separately

external_narratives.summary: IWM entry for the cross: location at the Dovecote Lane and High Street junction, description, inscription, size and condition. No maker, date, history or custodian given.
key_details: Junction of Dovecote Lane and High Street (B1043)

external_narratives.summary: IWM entry for the pillar in Holy Trinity churchyard: description, inscription, Clipsham stone, bronze plaque, unveiled and dedicated 7 May 2022. No maker or custodian given.

Newspaper report of the History Society's campaign: the crash, the crew, a bomb through a bathroom at Low Farm, and the planned steel Lancaster sculpture for Dovecote Lane. No date shown; the plan later changed.
key_details: Great Paxton History Society launched campaign
Original plan: steel sculpture on a stone in Dovecote Lane

external_narratives.summary: Report of the 7 May 2022 unveiling and dedication: local history society organised funding, planning and installation; Canon Annette Reed led the service; Father Peter Taylor dedicated it; relatives unveiled it; schoolchildren's poems; BBMF Spitfire flypast.
key_details: Dedicated by Father Peter Taylor, Hon. Padre of the 35/635 Squadron Association

external_narratives.summary: Society's own page: the memorial is in Holy Trinity churchyard, paid for by donations including a JustGiving appeal, unveiled 7 May 2022 with crew families present. The page does not mention the cross or maintenance.
key_details: Funded by local donations, crew families, businesses and a JustGiving appeal

external_narratives.summary: IBCC record for the navigator. Age and family not stated.
CWGC record for the navigator. No age listed. Only this CWGC page was fetched; the other six casualty numbers come from IBCC.
key_details: Ystalyfera (St David) Church Burial Ground, Llangiwg

Memorial page, updated May 2022: says the new memorial at Holy Trinity replaced one that had stood near the crash site for a number of years, shown in a photo labelled 'Up to May 2022'. It does not name the earlier memorial as a cross.
key_details: Replaced an earlier memorial near the crash site

cause_of_loss: Pilot lost control on take-off in fog, attributed to faulty instrument flying (AM Form 1180); aircraft struck trees and caught fire
